s1.syndrome_frame: Gradual onset of a painless, firm, and nonpulsatile mass in the thigh of a young child
salient_findings: Firm, nonpulsatile mass in the left medial thigh
Mass is fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin
CT scan shows a well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass with internal septations
MRI confirms a fatty-appearing, well-circumscribed mass with internal septations
key_facts: 18-month-old girl
Swelling in the left medial thigh
Mass has enlarged gradually over six months
Painless mass
No history of trauma or infection
Firm, nonpulsatile mass measuring approximately 10 cm
Fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin
No signs of inflammation, neurovascular impairment, or inguinal lymphadenopathy
Laboratory tests are unremarkable
CT scan shows a well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass in the left anteromedial compartment of the proximal thigh
MRI confirms a fatty-appearing, well-circumscribed mass with internal septations
Mass displaces the common and superficial femoral vessels anterolaterally without signs of invasion
Mass abuts the proximal femoral bone but does not erode it

shortlist.label: Lipoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Fatty-appearing mass with internal septations in a young child

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-circumscribed, fatty-appearing mass with no signs of invasion

shortlist.label: Myxoid liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypodense mass with internal septations, although rare in young children

shortlist.label: Lipomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple fatty masses, although not explicitly mentioned, remains a possibility

shortlist.label: Lipoblastomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to lipoblastoma, but with multiple lesions, remains a rare but plausible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's age, the gradual enlargement of the mass, and the imaging characteristics (well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass with internal septations and a density similar to subcutaneous fat) are consistent with lipoblastoma, a rare benign tumor that typically occurs in children under the age of 3.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipomas are less common in this age group and typically do not exhibit the same level of septation or rapid growth.

rejected.label: Myxoid liposarcoma
rejected.why: Myxoid liposarcomas are rare in children and usually have a more aggressive appearance on imaging.

rejected.label: Lipomatosis
rejected.why: Lipomatosis refers to a condition of multiple lipomas, which does not match the single, well-circumscribed mass described.

rejected.label: Lipoblastomatosis
rejected.why: Lipoblastomatosis is a diffuse form of lipoblastoma, which does not fit the well-circumscribed nature of the mass in this case.
